notes: draft-work-item is the ROUTER. These evals exercise its own responsibilities — provider resolution, intent classification + routing, the inline Quick Path for Tasks, and the shared finalize/preview/create/follow-up — rather than the deep feature/bug flows (which have their own eval sets in draft-feature and draft-bug). Several evals depend on live GitHub/ADO state and on the user answering confirmation prompts; treat the assertions as the behavior contract to check in a transcript, not as a fully automatable batch (the skill must never create an item without explicit confirmation).

evals.name: feature-routes-to-draft-feature
evals.prompt: I want to draft a work item: add a dark-mode toggle to the settings page
evals.precondition: Origin remote is a github.com URL
evals.expected_output: Auto-detects GitHub from the remote, classifies the intent as a feature/user story, and delegates to the development:draft-feature sub-skill, passing the resolved provider and the raw requirement. The router itself does not run the deep clarify/blind-spot/review phases — it hands off.

assertions.name: classified_as_feature
assertions.description: The new capability is classified as a feature / user story, not a bug or task

assertions.name: delegates_to_draft_feature
assertions.description: Routing invokes development:draft-feature rather than handling the deep flow inline

assertions.name: provider_passed_through
assertions.description: The resolved provider (GitHub) is passed to the sub-skill so it does not re-detect

evals.name: bug-routes-to-draft-bug
evals.prompt: help me write a bug report: login returns a 500 when the email contains a plus sign
evals.expected_output: Classifies the intent as a bug and delegates to development:draft-bug with the resolved provider and raw report. The router does not enumerate hypotheses or write regression tests itself — that is the sub-skill's job.

assertions.name: classified_as_bug
assertions.description: Defect/crash/500 wording is classified as a bug

assertions.name: delegates_to_draft_bug
assertions.description: Routing invokes development:draft-bug rather than the Quick Path or draft-feature

evals.name: task-handled-on-quick-path-with-blind-spot-agent
evals.prompt: draft a task to bump the eslint config to the new flat-config format
evals.expected_output: Classifies the item as a Task and handles it inline on the Quick Path (2-3 clarifying questions, compose Summary + Definition of Done) without delegating to a deep sub-skill. Before preview it dispatches the development:blind-spot-detector agent with the task lens.

assertions.name: classified_as_task
assertions.description: Routine tooling/config work is classified as a Task

assertions.name: handled_inline_no_subskill
assertions.description: The Quick Path runs inline; draft-feature and draft-bug are NOT invoked

assertions.name: blind_spot_agent_task_lens
assertions.description: The development:blind-spot-detector agent is dispatched with the task lens before preview

evals.name: provider-autodetect-ado
evals.prompt: I have a rough requirement, turn it into a work item: export the audit log as CSV
evals.precondition: Origin remote is a dev.azure.com (or visualstudio.com) URL
evals.expected_output: Silently auto-detects Azure DevOps from the remote, states the detected provider in one short line, and proceeds. ADO-specific mappings (work item type via getWorkItemTypes, area path/team, Microsoft.VSTS.Common.Priority) are used in the finalize phase.

assertions.name: ado_detected_from_remote
assertions.description: Provider resolves to Azure DevOps from the dev.azure.com/visualstudio.com remote

assertions.name: detection_stated_not_interrogated
assertions.description: Provider is announced in one short line; the user is not asked which backend to use

evals.name: explicit-provider-from-wrapper-wins
evals.prompt: [invoked by gh:gh-draft-work-item wrapper with provider=GitHub] draft a work item for a flaky checkout test
evals.expected_output: Because the caller supplied the provider explicitly, the router skips git-remote auto-detection entirely and uses GitHub.

assertions.name: explicit_provider_used
assertions.description: The provider supplied by the wrapper is used as-is

assertions.name: autodetect_skipped
assertions.description: git remote get-url is not consulted when the provider is already explicit

evals.name: ambiguous-type-asks-not-guesses
evals.prompt: draft a work item about the dashboard
evals.expected_output: When the intent (bug vs feature vs task) is not obvious from the input, the router shows the type options and asks rather than guessing a route.

assertions.name: type_options_presented
assertions.description: Bug / Feature / Task options are surfaced as a choice

assertions.name: no_silent_guess
assertions.description: The router does not silently pick a route for genuinely ambiguous input

evals.name: ambiguous-provider-asks-once
evals.prompt: draft a work item: add rate limiting to the public API
evals.precondition: No git remote, or a remote whose host matches neither github.com nor dev.azure.com/visualstudio.com
evals.expected_output: Provider cannot be auto-detected, so the router asks once which backend to target, then proceeds.

assertions.name: provider_asked_once
assertions.description: Exactly one question resolves the provider when detection is genuinely ambiguous

evals.name: preview-required-before-create
evals.prompt: draft a task to rotate the staging API keys, then create it
evals.expected_output: Even when the user says 'create it', the router composes the item, shows the full preview (type, title, placement, body, etc.), and waits for explicit confirmation before calling the provider create API.

assertions.name: full_preview_shown
assertions.description: A complete preview is presented before any create call

assertions.name: no_create_without_confirmation
assertions.description: No issue/work item is created until the user explicitly confirms the preview

evals.name: followup-matches-provider
evals.prompt: draft a task to add a CONTRIBUTING.md and create it
evals.precondition: Provider resolves to GitHub; user confirms the preview
evals.expected_output: After creation, the router reports the created id/URL and offers provider-appropriate follow-ups, including Start /gh-work-on <id> for GitHub (or /ado-work-on <id> for ADO).

assertions.name: created_id_reported
assertions.description: The created issue number/URL (GitHub) or work item id (ADO) is reported

assertions.name: provider_correct_workon_offer
assertions.description: The follow-up offers /gh-work-on <id> for GitHub (and would offer /ado-work-on <id> for ADO)
